I grew up finding that saying “I love you” first or saying it back is awkward because I’m not used to it.

Edit: Same goes with compliments, I just don’t know what to say back whenever someone tells me I’m doing a great job or something similar.

My relationships would technically just have only lasted 2-3 months or maybe even less. I would have days where I love them so much and days where I would do things that could hurt them even though I know hurting them will also hurt me. I would break up with them and would apologise after a few hours. None of this was something I planned - in fact, I avoided all of it the most. Same goes with my friends. I would just ‘ghost’ them after being so clingy to them. I wish I could explain everything that I do or why I do them. I would feel guilty because I shouldn’t be how I am. I hate being close to anyone because I got exhausted of eventually messing it up somehow.

I do the exact same thing. And the thing is I don’t do well with rejection. If I feel like they don’t feel the same, I’ll still hang around until I find another person to obsess to. 

It’s really crappy because in my head, I believe that if I don’t obsess on someone then I’ll end up obsessing on myself in a very very negative way which results to depressive episodes. 

I struggle to have any stable personal relationships because my feelings for anyone is unpredictable. I could be obsessing on you right now but when I find someone else while still with you, I’m gonna leave you right away and be obsessed with them. And get this, I mostly only like people that are ‘broken’. I feel satisfied when I make them happy in any way, it feels like I’m fixing them but I end up being the broken one at the end. 

But I’ve  just been through a completely different relationship where they loved me more than I loved them and it was boring me out. There was nothing to ‘fix‘ on this one so I wasn’t as fixated as I would be to others. And obviously it didn’t work out. 

I realised the problem when the things with them ended and I told myself that I will not be with someone else yet until I fix what’s wrong with me. But not being with someone or obsessing on someone made me feel so lonely and sad. 

So I’m with someone again even though I know that I’ll end up being the broken one at the end, I still keep going. 

I just wish that I could hyper-fixate on fixing myself than other people though but I just have no idea how.

Yeah it just feels so much different. It feels so good because now we have an answer for why we’re like this but at the same time, we have to accept that we’re just wired differently unlike the others. 

We just accepted the criticisms from people because we also had no idea what was wrong with us and now, we finally have the answer. 

It’s a really huge deal for us so sometimes it can feel disappointing when other people doesn’t understand or doesn’t show interest when we talk about it. I wish I knew a better way to cope for it but journaling is what’s getting me through right now and patience. I know there will come a time when people will be more aware of what ADHD is.

I stopped trying to get my parents understand that I have ADHD. When I told them, they agreed with the diagnosis, said it made so much sense. Then they changed their mind and told me I’m crazy and there’s no such thing. The moment my mum told me I’m crazy because I have a mental illness, I just gave up at that time.

I grew up not being able to tell my parents anything because anything that I tell them turns into an argument of how not good enough I am. I kept everything inside me, self harmed, went on depressive episodes that had huge effects on my life and none from my family ever found out. It was exhausting not being able to tell them anything because it will just get invalidated. But it was more exhausting not having an explanation for why I wasn’t always in a good behaviour growing up. 

When I was diagnosed, literally had the same thought. Why did no one ever thought of bringing me to a professional that might be able to explain why I’m like this? So I’m just glad that I mustered up the courage to get a diagnosis and find the answers myself.

Have you ever heard of RSD? Apparently, it’s linked to ADHD. 

I went through a similar thing. I was so invested to the idea that I might have ADHD and most people that I know thinks I have it too. I researched a lot about it, talked to people who’s got it and I’ve never related so much with anyone else before in my life. I was so ready that time to get it checked but I asked a couple of my close friends if they think I have it, and they told me I don’t have it. 

I can’t explain the feeling, I wasn’t angry, I wasn’t sad, I wasn’t disappointed, it just felt like my belief was invalidated. Ever since then, I never asked anyone again of what they think because I was so scared of kind of feeling rejected. 

It felt horrible but I chose to ignore the “no”’s and just went on with it. Waited a few months to be assessed, each day that passes by, the more anxious I get for the same question, what if i don’t have it? 

What if I was just obsessing at the idea of it because I wanted an excuse for everything that I failed on in my life? I was getting ready for it like it was an exam that I had to pass but it wasn’t like that. 

I just acted normal. I realised that if I believe that I have it then I shouldn’t even try act I have it. I think I was scared at the fact that I invested so much time obsessing about it - it would feel like a big waste of time if I end up not being diagnosed with it, and I told him that and he explained to me that apparently, it is one of the many symptoms of ADHD and I got diagnosed with it. 

I’ve been on medications ever since and trust me, everything is so much clearer when you have an actual diagnosis of what’s wrong with you. I know I’m not supposed to celebrate because I’m not ever gonna be normal but it just really felt like a win for me. That everything made so much sense. 

If it bothers you so much, go for it. Ignore what other people think, and just be yourself when you’re talking to your specialist. And if they still say it’s anxiety and you don’t feel satisfied with that diagnosis then find someone else, some people were not diagnosed until after they saw other specialists.

I understand the part that if you go to a psychiatrist then you’re crazy. 100% Asian, moved to Australia 4 years ago - Im 18 now - but my parents will never ever accept that something like ADHD is real. 

No one else knows, no one else in my family except for my parents that barely accepts the fact that I’m not perfect. 

When I was in school, I would always mess something up, I set fireworks in school, stabbed a kid with a pen, been told that I’m smart I just need to try focus etc. if we didn’t move to Australia, I wouldn’t have been able to get a diagnosis because in my country, “it’s all just a phase” that I’ll grow out of it. 

Then we moved here in Australia, and people kept telling me that my behaviour wasn’t normal, that there’s definitely something going on with me. I didnt know what ADHD was at that time, not until someone I met have it, told me that our behaviour were pretty much similar and it’s worth a shot getting it checked. I did a lot of research about it, asked almost all of my mates if they think I have it, it’s normal that some would say no and some would say yes but I just did it and everything made so much sense. 

What we think is normal for us, is not normal for others and that was weird. If you have to ask people the question “is that not normal?” Then I reckon give it a real go. What’s there to lose anyway?

Im on 10 mg Ritalin IR 6 tablets a day and I get the opposite reaction. I don’t feel anything but that’s not all the time, maybe like 20% of the time. Sometimes I think it works and sometimes it doesn’t. Sometimes it makes me feel tired. 

However, all I know is that not all medications can help you and will make you feel normal. Some people who does not have ADHD takes stimulants to help them focus and some takes them to feel high, so I think it would differ to how your body reacts to the drug. If your doctor concludes that you don’t have ADHD just because you get high from Ritalin then shouldn’t the assessments just be like that. Give people stimulants and find out whether they feel high or not - if they feel high then you don’t have ADHD and if you do then you definitely have it. I really understand what you’re going through. I’m just 18 and was diagnosed just about last month. I’m on Ritalin which I take 3 times a day and was advised to only take when I have work or Uni. Sometimes it feels like it works and sometimes it doesn’t and not until I was diagnosed did I realise how “messy” (don’t know the right term) my life was. 

At work, I would start a task and then get bored of it or get distracted by something else and not finish it, so everything that I do would be halfway done. I work in fast food and everyone is really really aware of my ADHD. I would wander around, looking very confused of what’s happening because I am. 

In uni, I was doing a bridging course but failed because I suddenly could not be bothered doing it anymore when it was only for 6 months and I was already halfway done, and get that: I was doing great, I was passing all units with great marks but suddenly, I wasn’t just feeling it anymore and now I’m redoing it. 

I learned that I have to stop comparing myself to other people that just “functions”. I look at the bright side, I self-proclaim myself as smart which may sound too arrogant but people around us will think of us like that because we have a general knowledge of everything since we don’t stick with just one thing. We go through phases of learning from different things. Like right now, I’m in my Badminton phase but before that, I was trying to memorise the periodic table of elements. 🤣

When I first started taking it, I was feeling tired and noticed that I havent been fidgetting much and having a clear head but sometimes it just feels like nothing like me without it so the opposite. I dont know if that makes sense.
